evidence: caller.js imported livekit-client from cdn.jsdelivr.net with no integrity mechanism on a page that collects an xi-api-key and mic access, contradicting web.rs's own embed-everything doctrine; the agent vendored the exact bytes with a provenance file as the reviewer proposed.
guidance_note: When a module states a doctrine (embed assets so nothing is fetched at runtime), apply it to every asset in the same PR, third-party dependencies included.

evidence: web.rs began with `use crate::api::AppState` while api::router() merged web::router(), a genuine two-way module dependency; the agent moved AppState to state.rs and assembly to app.rs exactly as proposed, and round 1 describes the cycle as gone.
guidance_note: Before a new module imports a type from the module that will mount it, place shared state in a lower module and do router assembly at the top.

evidence: The catch block's `await room.disconnect()` sits before `throw error`, so any rejection there replaces the original cause, which contradicts the comment's claim that 'the failure still travels'. The agent kept both errors (disconnect outcome appended, original as `cause`) rather than swallowing either; its claim that disconnect rejects on a never-connected room is not verifiable from the packet.
guidance_note: When writing cleanup inside a catch, check whether each cleanup step can itself throw before claiming the original error always propagates.

evidence: The shared click-handler catch set `call = null` and reset to 'join' on a failed leave as well as a failed join, so a failed disconnect looked like a successful one. Stopping the catch from mutating `call` and deriving the button from it is the reviewer's 'leave the button in an error state' option.
guidance_note: When one catch arm serves two operations, let each operation own its own state transition instead of having the catch assume one outcome for both.

evidence: mint() always set participant_name, and the server reads a present-but-empty value as Some(HappyUserId("")), so a blank field produced a metered call attributed to an empty user. The agent rejected 'omit when blank' because that would silently switch to the unmetered BYO path, and refused blank fields by name, extending the same check to agent_id.
guidance_note: Read form inputs through one parser that refuses blank required fields before any request is built, instead of passing raw .value strings to the API.

evidence: The README said 'three static files' while ASSETS embedded four. The agent corrected it and also counted the vendored SDK from F1's fix that landed in the same commit, so its own fix did not cause comment drift.
guidance_note: After splitting a file out, grep the docs for counts and file lists that describe the old layout.

evidence: `call.allowPlayback()` ran after `call` was assigned, and the catch nulled `call` without leave(), so a rejected startAudio orphaned a live room and mic. The agent removed the window by moving startAudio inside Call.join's existing teardown path, so no extra cleanup branch was needed.
guidance_note: Put every fallible step of acquiring a resource inside the constructor that already owns its teardown, so callers never hold a half-initialized object.

narrative: All seven findings were raised in round 0 against the original code. Every one was real. The agent took four with a better-shaped fix than the one proposed (error kept as cause, form parser, startAudio inside join, catch no longer owning state). Round 1 approved with no new findings, so none of the fixes caused another finding.
guidance_observations: Three of seven findings (F3, F4, F7) were the same family: async teardown and error paths in the browser client that left state inconsistent; one pass over every catch/cleanup path before opening the PR would have caught them together.
The agent checked F6's count against the vendored file from its own concurrent F1 fix, which is the move that prevents comment drift from fixes.

evidence: A moving `@v1` tag on an action that receives CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN is a real supply-chain exposure. However, the comment above the `uses:` line records the tag as a deliberate trade ('this repo tracks its latest release with no edit here, ever'), and the reviewer does not engage with it. The PR merged six seconds after it was created, so the thread was left unresolved with no reply.
guidance_note: Do not merge before the review lands; for installer-generated workflow files, answer a pinning finding on the thread and route any change to the generator rather than leaving it silent.

narrative: Single-file install of the generated code-review workflow, merged before its only review finished. The one finding, SHA-pinning the review action, has merit on security grounds but conflicts with a trade the template documents. It never got an answer.
guidance_observations: Merging at creation time means review findings arrive on a closed PR and go unanswered; even generated-file PRs should wait for the review and get a reply on each thread.

evidence: With the ParticipantConnected listener live during publishTrack/startAudio, an agent arriving in that window was announced by both the event and the roster sweep. The agent cited the vendored client's set-before-emit order and replaced both sources with a diff against the live roster, which also handles leave/rejoin.
guidance_note: When presence can be learned from both an event and a snapshot, derive the report from the single state (roster diff) instead of announcing from both triggers.

evidence: JSON.parse("null") returns null without throwing, so `stored[name]` crashed seedFields at module scope, despite a docstring promising a fallback. The agent's parser also drops non-string values like `{"apiKey":42}`, which the proposed null guard would have seeded into the form, and it showed the pre-fix behaviour failing its own check.
guidance_note: Treat localStorage as untrusted input and parse it into the exact shape the consumer needs (known keys, string values), not merely into a non-throwing shape.

narrative: Two real round-0 findings: a presence double-report race and a crash on a null stored value. In both cases the agent chose a stronger fix than the one proposed and showed it working (a live CDP run and a pre/post DOM-shim table). Round 1 approved with nothing new.
guidance_observations: Before choosing between the reviewer's options, the agent checked the vendored SDK's emit order. That evidence turned a dedupe patch into a single-source design.

evidence: look_up mixed the HTTP request with the max_input_tokens extraction, and that extraction had no test even though the whole budget rests on it. Commit 26f4aac extracted window_described_in(body, id) with three canned-body tests, which is the reviewer's proposal under a different name.
guidance_note: When a parse step is the one assumption a feature rests on, write it as a pure function with a fixture test in the original PR, not inline after the request.

evidence: Flag is a false positive. The overclaiming 'adds no startup dependency' doc comment was in the PR before review (1dd8d8e's '-' lines), and 26f4aac only extracted the parser. The reviewer was right that the comment conflated failure boundaries, and the agent rewrote it. The agent declined retry and the 4xx/5xx split because both arms exit non-zero to a supervisor, matching serve()'s fail-fast on the log and whisper model. The Nomad restart policy it relies on is not visible in the packet.
guidance_note: When a doc comment justifies a new startup dependency, state what failure boundary moved (an outage at restart now stops the process) instead of claiming nothing changed.

evidence: Flag is a false positive. BYTES_PER_TOKEN = 3 was added in the original PR revision, and 1dd8d8e touched only a doc comment. The conclusion holds (Korean measured 2.06 bytes/token, so the estimate undercounts), but the reviewer's 1-2 bytes/token figure and its Cyrillic claim were wrong per the agent's count_tokens table. The agent set the constant to 2 and committed the table.
guidance_note: When setting a heuristic constant on input that can be in any language (Whisper output), measure it across scripts before committing rather than justifying it from English alone.

narrative: Each of the three rounds that raised findings found one issue. Neither later finding was caused by a fix, despite the ON-NAMED-FIX-COMMIT flags: F2's overclaiming comment and F3's English-only constant were both in the original diff, and the fix commits named in the flags never touched them. The agent split F2 (fixed the comment, declined retry with a reasoned supervisor argument) and answered F3 with measurements instead of guessing.
guidance_observations: The reviewer surfaced pre-existing issues one per round, so the rounds cost review time even though no fix was faulty. The agent can only shorten that by self-reviewing every comment that justifies a trade and every magic constant before opening the PR.

evidence: The docstring promised a throw naming the field, but a present wrapper with an absent leaf returned undefined, which join(" ") turned into "". The agent added requireText at the leaf as proposed, kept absent separate from a legitimate "" transcript, and applied it to replies() too.
guidance_note: When a docstring promises a loud failure on malformed input, test the leaf-missing shape as well as the wrapper-missing one before claiming it.

evidence: stt-acceptance re-spelled `user_transcription_event` in the very PR that claimed to centralize it. The agent showed the proposed transcriptEventIds() would either crash the event_id check or return undefined, and exposed the unparsed payload via transcriptEvents() instead.
guidance_note: When centralizing a wire-shape key, grep the whole PR for the key string before writing the 'one owner' claim.

evidence: F1's requireText (7bff620) made transcripts()/replies() throw inside waitFor predicates. That made waitFor's docstring ('Returns a boolean rather than throwing') false. Crashing on a malformed protocol event with the field named is a defensible design, not a bug, so the agent kept the behaviour and corrected the docstring in 839941d.
guidance_note: When a fix makes an accessor throw, grep its callers in the same commit and update every docstring that promised they never throw.

evidence: This is the same consequence as F3 at llm-acceptance's first-message waitFor: replies() throws via requireText from F1's fix. The agent handled it the same way, with one docstring correction and no behaviour change.
guidance_note: Sweep every call site of an accessor whose contract a fix just changed, including sites that use it as a polling predicate.

evidence: Flag is a false positive. The 'vad-, tools-, and inbound-text-acceptance ... remaining copies' sentence is verbatim in the round-0 docstring (F1's hunk), and 7bff620 only moved it onto transcriptEvents(). The agent confirmed the grep and moved the note to replies(), where the duplication actually is.
guidance_note: Produce any 'remaining copies' list in a comment from a grep for the exact key, not from memory of which scripts touch controlEvents.

evidence: It is true that the checks.record detail argument calls a throwing accessor unconditionally; that only became possible with F1's requireText. A malformed event ending the run with the field named is the intended design. The proposed try/catch fallback would bury a wire-format bug in a detail string under a green tally, so declining was right.

Flag is a false positive. The 'every settled transcript' join comment and the first-final wait both predate review, and 7bff620 only swapped settled() for transcriptEvents(). The agent confirmed the split is real (['Hello','Bye.']) and replaced the wait with a quiescence window, which was one of the reviewer's suggestions.
guidance_note: When a comment claims a value is complete (all finals joined), check that the wait feeding it actually waits for completeness.

evidence: F1's fix (7bff620) added requireText, and the reply claimed 'Covered by a check over every malformed shape', but that check lived in a scratchpad outside the repo. The agent admitted this, committed caller.test.mjs under node --test in 4c60e91, and showed by mutation that the test can fail.
guidance_note: Commit the test a fix reply cites in the same fix commit; never claim coverage from a file outside the repo.

evidence: This duplicates F8 from the same round: no test for requireText's four boundary cases exists in the tree despite the F1 reply's coverage claim. The same 4c60e91 test file closed it.
guidance_note: Commit the test a fix reply cites in the same fix commit; never claim coverage from a file outside the repo.

narrative: F1's fix (requireText) is the root of five later findings. Three are about its new throwing contract reaching waitFor predicates and detail arguments, and waitFor's docstring had become false. Two are about the test its reply claimed but never committed. The agent kept the throw as a deliberate design, which is defensible, and corrected the docstring. Round 2 consisted entirely of the missing-test findings, so a complete F1 fix would have saved it. F5 and F7 were flagged as post-review but sit on text carried unchanged from round 0.
guidance_observations: Changing an accessor's failure contract needs a same-commit sweep of its callers and of every docstring that described the old contract.
A fix reply that claims verification has to point at an artifact in the repo; claiming scratchpad coverage cost a full review round.

evidence: The drop guard is declared after `listening`, so it cancels before the channel closes with nothing awaited between them, and the flush+transcribe is wasted on the ordinary hang-up path. The agent took the reviewer's 'skip the flush when exiting via cancellation' option and encoded it as Next/Ending, with two tests.
guidance_note: When adding a second way for a loop to end, carry the reason out of the loop as a value before writing any post-loop work that only one of the endings is owed.

evidence: The new Arriving info lines had no conversation id although listen() runs per call in a shared process. Instead of threading the id through Ear/Arriving as proposed, the agent wrapped the spawned future in an info_span, which also covers the trace line, and showed live log lines carrying conversation=.
guidance_note: When adding telemetry inside a per-call spawned task, attach the call's identity as a span at the spawn site in the same change.

evidence: This duplicates F2: none of the listen() logs carried a conversation id. The fix was the same info_span at the spawn site in lib.rs, not the proposed parameter threading.
guidance_note: When adding telemetry inside a per-call spawned task, attach the call's identity as a span at the spawn site in the same change.

evidence: Changing `return` to `break` made the dead-channel exits fall through to flush+transcribe for a result nobody can receive. The reviewer suggested tracking the exit reason, and the agent did exactly that with Ending::NobodyListening, keeping arriving.report() on every exit.
guidance_note: When widening an early return into a break so shared tail code runs, list what the tail does and gate the parts that only some exits are owed.

evidence: The reviewer hedged on whether dropping the RemoteAudioTrack wrapper stops the stream. The agent cites livekit-0.8.3 `rtc_track()` returning an owned clone stored by NativeAudioStream, and reports about 40 live calls with heard_ms up to 51,410. The livekit source is not in the packet, so the pushback rests on claims this audit cannot check, though they are specific and consistent.

This duplicates F4: once the control channel is closed, a break falls through to a discarded Whisper transcription. The same Ending discriminant in 03ca4b3 skips the flush on NobodyListening, as the reviewer suggested.
guidance_note: When widening an early return into a break so shared tail code runs, list what the tail does and gate the parts that only some exits are owed.

evidence: This is the same missing conversation id on the Arriving lines. This reviewer instance explicitly offered 'wrap the spawned listen() future in a tracing::info_span!(conversation = ...)', which is the fix the agent made.
guidance_note: When adding telemetry inside a per-call spawned task, attach the call's identity as a span at the spawn site in the same change.

evidence: Turning on openconv_agent=info by default exposed two warn! sites that logged raw transcript text and reply text. The agent switched both to `chars = len()`, matching the module's existing pattern. This fix swept only the two named sites (see F12).
guidance_note: When a default log filter newly enables a target, grep every log call in that target for raw content fields before shipping the filter change.

evidence: 03ca4b3 inserted `enum Next`/`Ending` between next_frame's old doc ('the flush and the report after it happen on both') and the function, leaving that stale doc attached to Next. 60b36a8 deleted the stale lines.
guidance_note: When inserting new items between a doc comment and the function it documents, move or rewrite that doc in the same edit and reread every doc block above the insertion.

evidence: The orphaned doc left by 03ca4b3 says the flush runs on both endings. That is the opposite of the F1 fix's `NobodyListening => None`, and it invites restoring the waste. The same stale lines as F9 were deleted in 60b36a8.
guidance_note: When inserting new items between a doc comment and the function it documents, move or rewrite that doc in the same edit and reread every doc block above the insertion.

evidence: This is a third report of the misplaced next_frame doc that 03ca4b3 left on `enum Next`, duplicating the `biased` paragraph. It was closed by the same deletion in 60b36a8.
guidance_note: When inserting new items between a doc comment and the function it documents, move or rewrite that doc in the same edit and reread every doc block above the insertion.

evidence: F8's fix in 03ca4b3 redacted the two warn! sites the reviewer named but left decode_client_event logging 200 raw payload characters. That is the same leak class, exposed by the same default-filter change. The agent replaced `raw` with `chars = payload.len()` in 60b36a8 and admitted it was 'missed for the same reason'.
guidance_note: When fixing one instance of a leak class, grep the whole newly-enabled target for every field of that class instead of fixing only the sites the reviewer listed.

evidence: Flag is a false positive. The `fn max` to `pub fn max` widening is in the original PR revision (round 0 summary: 'exposes Score::max'), and 03ca4b3 did not touch vad.rs. The only caller is in-crate, so pub(crate) was right, and 60b36a8 applied it.
guidance_note: When widening a private item for a new caller, pick the narrowest visibility that reaches that caller (pub(crate) for in-crate) in the original change.

evidence: Flag is a false positive. DEFAULT_LOG was in the original PR, and 60b36a8 did not touch main.rs. On the merits, tracing-subscriber's default `tracing-log` feature is on (Cargo.toml adds env-filter without default-features=false), and its init() installs LogTracer. The agent showed this with source and a throwaway crate where log::warn! from libwebrtc/livekit printed while filtered records were suppressed.

narrative: Round 0 raised eight findings, mostly real: the wasted flush on hang-up, missing call ids, and raw content in newly-enabled logs. They were fixed in 03ca4b3, mostly with better-shaped fixes. That commit caused four round-1 findings: a stale doc left on `enum Next` (reported three times) and a third raw-payload log site the F8 sweep missed. Round 1 would still have run, because it also caught the pre-existing pub Score::max. Round 2's lone finding (the log bridge) was wrong and correctly declined with a run.
guidance_observations: Both fix-caused misses in 03ca4b3 come from fixing only the named site: the doc comment above an insertion point and the sibling log calls in the same target were one grep away.
The two pushbacks (F5, F14) cited specific crate source lines plus empirical runs; the F14 throwaway-crate run turned a confident-sounding wrong finding into a checkable rejection.
